newsitem.title: USA: US High Court to hear Lincoln Savings-related case.
newsitem.headline: US High Court to hear Lincoln Savings-related case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court said Monday it would decide whether a lawsuit arising from the litigation over the collapse of Lincoln Savings and Loan should be tried in Arizona or in Illinois, where it was filed.
The lawsuit had been brought by Lexecon Inc, a privately held law and economics consulting firm that prepared several reports for Lincoln in 1987 and 1988.

Lexecon was named as a defendant in lawsuits brought by a class of investors who lost money in Lincoln's collapse. Those lawsuits were consolidated and heard in federal court in Arizona. The claims against Lexecon later were resolved.

Lexecon in 1992 sued in federal court in Illinois, charging malicious prosecution and defamation against several of the attorneys representing the investors. The lawsuit charged the attorneys had a personal vendetta against the firm.
A judicial panel ordered the case transferred from Illinois to Arizona. The judge who heard the Lincoln litigation removed himself from considering the lawsuit, and it was assigned to another judge.
After pre-trial proceedings, Lexecon moved to have the case sent back to Illinois for trial, a request that was denied. The judge then dismissed the claims, a ruling upheld by a U.S. appeals court.

The Supreme Court will decide whether the judge should have sent the case back to Illinois for trial. Arguments in the case will be heard during the high court term that begins in October, with a decision likely early next year.
